correctness.rationale: I generated lines as closures of point pairs under the four field scalars, then grouped them by their translation subspaces. Scanning all 2^16 named assignments, all accepted pairs and breadth-first search from each state independently reproduced the five unique balanced-direction classes of size 24, pair counts 2880/1320/2880/60 at Hamming distances 6/8/10/16, common-neighbor counts 22/24/14/0 in G6, spheres (1,48,70,1), unique complement antipodes, and five exactly-eight components K24 minus a matching. In the quadratic proof, the two quotient maps for distinct directions jointly form an isomorphism because their kernels intersect trivially, so the sum has the direct sum of two nonsingular two-dimensional polar forms. The complete finite replay also establishes the claims without relying on the cited static census.
residual_risks: Order four only with named colors and proper batch endpoints; no requirement of proper intermediate single flips. The common-neighbor certificate is finite exhaustion, not a formal verification artifact.

value.rationale: These are the valid splittings of a classical affine plane whose static geometry was known, so the number of points that must change to reach another splitting is a natural reconfiguration invariant. The sharp minimum batch size, unique complement at distance three, and disconnection for exactly-eight moves answer distinct reachability questions; the common-neighbor table describes the alternative two-step routes.
residual_risks: No higher-order affine-plane theorem or algorithmic scaling claim.
